description: Identifying Areas of High Salinity in the Pecos River Basin is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by USFWS, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. Over the years, increased salinity of the Pecos River has become a major concern among water users and water managers. Although many studies have contributed to the understanding of salinity increases in the basin, managers and researchers identified the need for consistent sampling of the same constituents at the same sites along the Pecos River. Coverage: Pecos River, Texas (2021). The toolkit gives Pecos River, Texas as the location, 2021 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
